descripcion: This zone is very close to Route 307, requiring a short walk and river crossing to reach it. It was developed in 2019 and has 8 routes spread across 3 nearby sectors. It sits at almost 3000m altitude. The predominant rock is granite. Like all zones near the Abra del Infiernillo, it is a great option when bad weather prevents climbing in the Tafí Valley.
llegar: From the Abra del Infiernillo, continue along Route 307 for approximately 5 km until you reach the parking point. From there, the walk takes you down to the Amaicha river, which you follow upstream for about 100m, then turn right and continue up the secondary gorge that appears. There you will find the 'Pasillo' sector first, then 'Mogote'. The 'Cuevita' sector is above 'Pasillo', on the hillside.
sectorAcampe: There is no defined area yet. With some imagination you can find a flat spot near the river. Drinking river water without prior treatment is not recommended, as there are settlements with many animals upstream.

descripcion:
This is the zone with the highest number of routes and the most visited, due to its wide range of grades and proximity to Route 325.
It has several sectors that served as the setting for a route-setting course managed by the AAM in 2016, where most of the current routes were developed, and it mainly features short but overhanging routes.
This sector is also known by the names: Mirador del Cóndor, Peñón del Águila, Las Carreras, Calavera and others.
llegar:
Route 325 is an unpaved mountain tourist road connecting the towns of Tafí del Valle and El Mollar, crossing the Las Carreras valley and skirting Cerro El Pelao.
From El Mollar, take Route 325 toward the village of El Rincón, continue through it until you cross the El Mollar River, where you should leave your vehicle. From this point, walk uphill toward the sectors. If you continue 600m along the route, as if heading toward the Mirador del Cóndor, you reach the La Escuelita sector.
sectorAcampe: You can camp in the gorge, by the river, or at Don Romano's post at the Mirador del Cóndor.

descripcion: Developed in 2021, this is one of the most beautiful sectors in the valley, located in an alder forest with a small waterfall dividing the wall. There are 5 routes from 6b to 7b+ and it is generally in the shade.
llegar: From El Mollar, follow Route 325 toward Tafí del Valle. A short distance from where the El Rincón village ends, after passing a house where adobe bricks are made (Adobera Ibañez) and around the bend, you will find the parking area. There is a shrine to the Virgin of the Valley on the other side of the road, and you should walk 5 minutes following the path uphill along the right bank (N) of the gorge.
sectorAcampe: You can camp next to your vehicle. The available water does not inspire confidence for drinking.

descripcion: This is the second sector with the most routes and also the newest. It started being developed in 2022 and features several types of rock of varying quality, with the wall known as 'Paraíso' being the highlight (this zone is also known by that name). These sectors owe their importance to being an alternative when bad weather prevents climbing in the Tafí Valley, as clouds cannot pass the Abra del Infiernillo. It is located at 2900 masl.
llegar: From Tafí del Valle, follow Route 307 toward Amaicha del Valle. 8km past the Abra del Infiernillo you will find the parking point (caution is advised when driving through this area due to dense fog). From here, a trail marked with cairns descends to the Amaicha river, crosses it, then climbs to the sectors. The walk takes approximately 30 minutes. During the rainiest time of year (summer), the river may have more flow, so it is recommended to cross carefully — it is better to take off your shoes and get wet than to look for a jumping point.
sectorAcampe: While there is no defined area, there is a comfortable camping spot a few meters upstream (from the river crossing point), on the same side as the trail on a flat platform. Drinking river water without prior treatment is not recommended, as there are settlements with many animals upstream.

descripcion:
As the name suggests, these are the first routes developed in the Tafí Valley (1997), and the walk takes approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour to reach them. They are characterized by a slightly overhanging technical slab.
The wall is generally in the shade all day and has 3 graded routes plus a 5th-grade warm-up.
llegar: The best access is from Tafí del Valle following Route 325. In the Rodeo Grande neighbourhood, at the level of the San Isidro Labrador chapel, turn toward the slopes of Cerro Muñoz (to the right) and continue along an internal road to its end, right over a stream. From this point, cross a gate and continue walking up the gorge until you reach the routes.
sectorAcampe: Not recommended. There is water flowing weakly through the gorge.

descripcion: This is a sector that offers magnificent views while climbing, as it is located on the eastern slopes of Cerro Pelao, facing the La Angostura Dam. In addition to the bolted routes, it has some top-rope routes and some bouldering, and while it is very beginner-friendly, it features a proposed 8a line... the route that names the sector and was the first route developed here, in 2006.
llegar: From Tafí del Valle, take the road toward the Ojo de Agua neighbourhood, passing near the cemetery and following the La Angostura Dam along its western bank toward Casas Viejas (on Route 307, the Casas Viejas sign can be used as a reference). At the marked point, turn right and continue along a dirt track that comes very close to the sector. From there, just follow the path for 5 minutes and cross a gate to reach the routes.
sectorAcampe: Near the sector there are some flat spots for camping. The available water, depending on where it is obtained, may or may not be drinkable.

descripcion:
This sector is at high altitude and 1:30 hours of walking away, which is why it is not often visited. It also only has two sport climbing routes, long and on a slightly positive slab, bolted in 2012. Both routes are around 6c grade, and visiting them requires consideration of the isolation, harsh sun and altitude effects. Continuing up the gorge at 3700 masl you reach the 'Rocódromo', a classic spot for traditional climbing.
Unlike the other climbing zones, this one is located in the Cumbres Calchaquíes, within the homonymous Provincial Park (P.P.C.C.).
llegar: From Tafí del Valle, follow Route 307 toward the Abra del Infiernillo. A few kilometers before reaching it, you will find the entrance to the P.P.C.C. where there is a building. From there you must walk approximately 1:30 hr to reach the sport climbing sector, passing first through the Diaz family's post. From the house, follow the river along its right bank until you reach the routes. To reach the Rocódromo, continue up the gorge (3 hours of walking).
sectorAcampe: Camping near the sport climbing sector is not recommended. The gorge water is drinkable. At the Rocódromo, the camping area is defined next to a large rock with an overhang and stone walls.

descripcion: Sector located at the foot of Cerro Ñuñorco, mainly bouldering with some routes. It is set in the gorge, with boulders distributed on both sides. All proposed boulders have a very pleasant approach and there is generally space at the base of the routes. Little shade and in summer the sun is unforgiving. Not all the bolts and anchors are in the best condition.
llegar: From El Mollar, continue along Route 307 toward La Angostura, that is, toward the dam wall. Before reaching it, there is a bus stop with a sign reading 'Ñuñorco', where you should turn and begin climbing. Continue along this dirt road to its end, near some houses and a water intake. To reach the sector, just walk 5 minutes toward the gorge. For reference, the rocks start at the level of the tanks and pools, and you must ascend through the gorge to find the various boulders.
sectorAcampe: Not recommended. The gorge carries water.
